body:
## Problem and authorized task

The complete MSE-001 design and executable reference were preserved only as a downloadable review package. GitHub held the coordination review, so later workers could not recover all source, contracts, findings and verification from the MOTHER repository.

Chad's instruction: “The prototype needs to be saved to the mother repository.  All documentation and findings along with any new design details we need to add at this time.”

## What this PR saves

- The original release at `research/mse/reference-v0.1.0/`: 63 payload files plus its manifest, byte-for-byte preserved. This includes all A–I deliverables, prototype code/tests, draft contracts and examples, proposed SQL, evidence, three patches, installation/retirement tools and original release history.
- `docs/mse/` as the current entry point: current repository reconciliation and integration addendum, the historical coordination review, additional scientific/source notes, installation instructions, change log, release notes, import report and independent publication review.
- Explicit proposed contracts for source revisions, availability/coverage, immutable evidence snapshots, state uncertainty, specialist/federation compatibility, conditional mechanism/receptor modeling, measurement requests, intervention/exposure/outcome separation and successor memory preserving failures and contradictions.
- A failure-propagating verifier and scoped MSE workflow. The preserved release is excluded from format-rewriting hooks and is protected by its original manifest; root pytest does not collect the isolated reference tests.
- A source-bound repository-context handoff is recorded as the follow-up publication metadata commit.

## Verification actually run

- Original archive/extracted/imported content comparison: all 64 files match; 895,441 bytes preserved.
- `python3 -B tools/verify_mse_reference.py --all`: PASS — 56 prototype tests, 25 contract checks, seven in-memory SQL checks, and three exact patch reconstructions.
- Extra-file, changed-payload and changed-manifest probes: rejected as expected.
- Existing context-reader suite: 50 tests passed.
- Scoped pytest collection: no prototype tests collected by root discovery, expected exit 5.
- Black 25.9.0, Ruff 0.13.1 and YAML/JSON checks passed for new integration tooling/configuration.
- Independent scientific/publication review: no blocking findings within its stated scope.
- GitHub source commit readback: all 84 publication file blobs/modes match the prepared files; unrelated base files are preserved.

Original archive SHA-256: `e6f2a0c1d5fea4eb6fc27c93d0261dac7729e180164cac7faf863cb3acbd2fee`. Original manifest SHA-256: `112ccb8df17d6afc6d8b7f932fbdeac31b1663ccd04c5538b9bd9a32e94a25f1`.

## Scope and limits

The executable reference remains retrospective HR/log-SDNN signal-deviation modeling with fixed, uncalibrated parameters. New glucose/federation/graph adapters are proposed, not implemented. Software tests establish neither biological observability nor individual intervention efficacy.

The current NAS-glucose hold remains in force. No production service, data, credentials, device signing, model weights, Research Scout 2.0 or weekly Meta-Research schedule is changed. MOTHER is public; fixtures are synthetic and publication review found no raw private health exports or credentials. Historical technical provenance metadata is retained.

## Source and handoff

Initial source commit: `18f7b040b576294de6570ce6e8247e8ed8590caf`, based on `818426fe90fab1bfd9583640363d4001b30e633f`.

Start at [`docs/mse/README.md`](../blob/work/mse-001-reference-and-design-20261119/docs/mse/README.md). Exact commands and non-deleting retirement are in `docs/mse/INSTALL.md`. The original three standalone patches remain under the preserved release.

REPORT-ID: MSE-001-PUBLICATION-20261119-R1. Status: source publication completed, draft review pending; no merge or deployment claim. Remote CI is checked separately at its exact head. Next action: review this preservation PR; select any later adapter implementation as a separate scoped task.
